cassette: none: reducer.PostgresAWSCloudRuntimeDriftWriter is a Postgres fact writer, not a Cypher graph writer, and operates over flat model.Candidate values, not a CanonicalMaterialization; the two fixture candidates live inline in go/internal/replay/costcounting/aws_cloud_runtime_drift_cost_test.go
description: Two admitted aws_cloud_runtime_drift candidates (orphaned + unmanaged cloud resource) in one scope, driven through the production Postgres fact writer over an InstrumentedDB-wrapped counting queryer. #5848 made WriteAWSCloudRuntimeDriftFindings transactional -- an insert-admission check (rejects a pass whose evidence-read watermark is older than one already admitted for the same scope/generation), the shared reducerBatchInsertVersionedFacts bounded chunked bulk insert (go/internal/reducer/reducer_fact_batch_insert.go, batch size 1000, issue #5317), and a generation-authoritative retire that removes a stale finding for a reclassified or converged ARN -- so one Write call now costs exactly 3 statements instead of 1 (raised from budget=1 on 2026-07-29, measured: 3 observations before this change would have been 0 due to an adjacent InstrumentedDB.Begin instrumentation gap this same change closed). Two negative controls guard this: a duplicate-invocation control (same candidate set written twice, 6 observations) and a within-call N+1 control (one candidate per Write call, 6 observations) both exceed this tightened budget.
